solutions.latex:
The region from $x=-2$ to $x=0$ (between the line and $y=-x$):

$$\begin{aligned} A_1&=\int_{-2}^0\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x+3-(-x)\right)dx\\ &=\int_{-2}^0\left(\dfrac{3}{2}x+3\right)dx\\ &=\left[\dfrac{3x^2}{4}+3x\right]_{-2}^0\\ &=0-\left(\dfrac{3(-2)^2}{4}+3(-2)\right)\\ &=3 \end{aligned}$$

(Or as a triangle, $A_1=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 3\times 2=3$.)

So $7$ square units more are needed for $x$ from $0$ to $k$. The whole triangle from $x=0$ to $x=6$ has area $\dfrac{1}{2}\times 3\times 6=9>7$, so $k<6$.

$$\begin{aligned} 7&=\int_0^k\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x+3-x\right)dx\\ 7&=\int_0^k\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x+3\right)dx\\ 7&=\left[-\dfrac{1}{4}x^2+3x\right]_0^k\\ 7&=-\dfrac{1}{4}k^2+3k\\ k^2-12k+28&=0\\ (k-6)^2&=8\\ k&=6\pm 2\sqrt{2} \end{aligned}$$

But $k<6$:

$$\therefore\ k=6-2\sqrt{2}$$

solutions.latex:
For the $y$ intercept, substitute $x=0$: $y=-3$.

$$y'=3x^2-12x+9$$

For stationary points, $y'=0$:

$$\begin{aligned} 3x^2-12x+9&=0\\ x^2-4x+3&=0\\ (x-3)(x-1)&=0 \end{aligned}$$

$x=3$, $y=-3$ or $x=1$, $y=1$.

$$y''=6x-12$$

When $x=3$, $y''=6(3)-12=6>0$ (concave up), so there is a minimum turning point at $(3,-3)$.

When $x=1$, $y''=6(1)-12=-6<0$ (concave down), so there is a maximum turning point at $(1,1)$.

For possible points of inflection, $y''=0$: $6x-12=0$, so $x=2$, $y=-1$.

Check for concavity:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 2 & 3\\\hline y'' & -6 & 0 & 6\\\hline\end{array}$$

Concavity changes, so there is a point of inflection at $(2,-1)$.

solutions.latex:
The tangent passes through $(0,-c)$:

$$\begin{aligned} -c&=-c\sec^2 c+\tan c\\ -c&=-c(1+\tan^2 c)+\tan c\\ -c&=-c-c\tan^2 c+\tan c\\ c\tan^2 c-\tan c&=0\\ \tan c\,(c\tan c-1)&=0 \end{aligned}$$

$\tan c=0$ gives $c=0$, not possible since $c\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. So $\tan c=\dfrac{1}{c}$.

$$\begin{aligned} \tan^2 c&=\dfrac{1}{c^2}\\ 1+\tan^2 c&=\dfrac{1}{c^2}+1\\ \sec^2 c&=\dfrac{1+c^2}{c^2} \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ \text{gradient}=\dfrac{c^2+1}{c^2}$$

Alternative: from $\tan c=\dfrac{1}{c}$ and the points $(0,-c)$, $(c,\tan c)$,

$$\begin{aligned} m&=\dfrac{\tan c+c}{c-0}\\ &=\dfrac{\frac{1}{c}+c}{c}\\ &=\dfrac{1+c^2}{c}\times\dfrac{1}{c}\\ &=\dfrac{1+c^2}{c^2} \end{aligned}$$
